title: B.C. premier to be sworn in, announce cabinet at Government House
summary: Lorne Doerkson will be sworn in on Friday as B.C.'s 38th premier by Lt.-Gov. Wendy Cocchia, alongside his cabinet.

image.caption: Lorne Doerkson will be sworn in as B.C.'s 38th premier, along with his Conservative cabinet, on Friday. (Chad Hipolito/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Lorne Doerkson will be sworn in on Friday as B.C.'s 38th premier by Lt.-Gov. Wendy Cocchia, alongside his cabinet.
The ceremony will take place at Government House starting at 11 a.m. PT
The ceremony will take place at Government House in Victoria, starting at 11 a.m. PT.
Among the invited guests is former B.C. Conservative leader John Rustad.

"The hardest job any premier does is to create a cabinet, because the majority of people that go into cabinet didn't necessarily get what they wanted, and the majority of people that didn't go into cabinet would have loved to have been there," he said.
While Rustad expects this cabinet will have fewer ministries than the former B.C. NDP government, there are a few new ministries that may be created.
Doerkson has talked about appointing a minister to reduce red tape, and to cut permitting times for major resource projects.

B.C. Lt.-Gov. Wendy Cocchia is seen at the legislature on Feb. 12, 2026. She will lead a swearing-in ceremony for the province's next premier, Lorne Doerkson, on Friday. (Chad Hipolito/The Canadian Press)
It is the first time the B.C. Conservative Party has been elected to government in more than 100 years.
The Conservatives' majority, the largest the province has seen in 25 years, comes in the wake of a snap election called by former NDP premier David Eby last month.
When the NDP formed government in 2017, after a confidence agreement with the B.C. Greens, there were no Conservative MLAs in the legislature.

blocks.text: On Thursday, 63 B.C. Conservative MLAs were sworn in — with one to take their oath of office pending a judicial recount next week.
Doerkson has said there will not be a fall legislative session, in order to give his new cabinet members time to familiarize themselves with their new files.
